# A17′ — Traversal with Return

<!-- paired-field-navigation -->
[Argument field](../README.md) · [Other face: A17 — Toroidal Circulation and the Arche-Topos](../A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos.md) · [Shared A/C root](AC.md)
<!-- /paired-field-navigation -->

## #0 — The model enters what it models

A simulation can become an event in the world it represents. A prediction informs an action; the action changes what happens; the changed situation supplies the next model with different conditions. In [Bratton's real-to-sim-to-real scenario](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q022), descriptive, predictive and speculative models have different relations to what their use brings about. The sequence can involve one coordinating actor or many actors whose models and actions meet without their knowing the whole chain.

A [returning passage](../A17-Toroidal-Circulation-and-the-Arche-Topos.md) can retain a difference even when it reaches the same address. In a relay the precise question is which difference survives: an outcome, an intervention, a path of decisions or the conditions under which the work was entrusted? The technological answer has to be given in the relations of the actual relay. A model, an action and the conditions of another model can form a returning circuit without possessing the topology of a torus. Their consequence is already substantial: a representation helps constitute what a subsequent representation will encounter.

## #1 — Three uses of a formed world

Describing, predicting and exploring possibilities entrust different work to a model. A descriptive model is tested against the relevant state or process. A predictive model anticipates a later event and can inform an action that realises, prevents or accommodates it. A speculative model can disclose a course not previously considered. Its contribution may be a possibility worth investigating rather than a forecast to accept. These are the distinct modalities in [the brief's §5.2](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md).

Consider a constructed greenhouse relay. Measurements of temperature enter a model; a forecast of afternoon heat leads a controller to open a vent; later measurements return. The achieved temperature is partly a consequence of acting on the prediction. Comparing it with the prediction must therefore retain the intervention. A forecast of excessive heat is not refuted merely because the action it prompted prevented that heat.

The model's inherited world includes more than readings. It includes a time horizon, an account of how vent position affects temperature, a target range and permission to actuate the vent. Each relation changes what can be inferred or done. Recording them makes it possible to distinguish an erroneous observation from an inadequate model, an unsuitable target or an action never authorised. The meaningful unit is the whole passage through these conditions.

## #2 — What the return must retain

On the torus a winding pair retains a path's class. It does not retain every turn, pause or encounter. A technical relay requires the same discrimination among kinds of record. A statement that the system returned to a familiar temperature says little about the sources it consulted, the action it took or the criterion under which the outcome counted as successful. A summary can be accurate at its own grain while insufficient for another question.

For the greenhouse, retain the observations and their times, the forecast and its conditions, the proposed intervention, the act actually performed and the subsequent measurements. The returned encounter can then correct different things. A misplaced sensor calls for a corrected observation route. An inaccurate response estimate calls for a changed model. A target appropriate to the old planting may be unsuitable for the new one. A controller lacking permission to operate the vent needs a decision from the office holding that permission, not another confident sentence about temperature.

A retained route must therefore reach the particular condition it claims to revise. Some conditions may be available to the local controller; others belong to a supplier, maintainer or commissioner. Identifying the latter preserves a real dependency even before it can be changed. [The direction of dependence](A34-prime-Direction-of-Dependence.md) distinguishes that practical authority from the capacity to represent a change.

## #3 — The relay grows around its own effects

Once the intervention changes the greenhouse, the next model inherits a world partly formed by the preceding model. Another actor may model that controller's behaviour; the controller may in turn respond to that actor. In Bratton's §5.3–5.4, simulations of different resolutions become one another's objects and conditions through this deepening chain. Their sequence need not form a single hierarchy of increasingly complete pictures.

The relation introduces specific possibilities of error. A later model may inherit a measurement stripped of the intervention that produced it. A summary may preserve the result while losing the purpose under which it was sought. A counter-model may exploit that omission. The brief's ninth research question asks how such relay economies produce value, decay or deception. Those alternatives are questions about what occurs in the passages, not names for closed and open loops. A fully documented relay can still pursue a destructive purpose; a useful offline simulation can illuminate a possibility before any feedback circuit has been built.

The [symbolic linker](A14-prime-Code-as-the-Ages-Logos.md) keeps a representation related to what it signifies without making the represented world identical with its present model. Returning information is valuable because it can alter the relation. Merely recirculating the same interpretation may give an error more occasions to repeat.

## #4 — A revised criterion, an altered commission

An operational return makes a later act inherit what was learned. In the greenhouse, a corrected response model changes the next vent adjustment. A deeper return asks whether the target itself should still govern: the plants have changed, the use of the building has changed, or an overlooked consequence has become relevant. Altering a forecast under a fixed objective and revising the objective are different transformations.

The sourceward movement becomes explicit when a returned encounter can reach the commission. The operator who requested a stable temperature may discover that the request excluded the humidity on which the plants depend. The correction then concerns the account of the task, not just the means of meeting it. Its effects must enter the next enacted configuration to become more than an amended description. The operator's judgment and the authority to enact it must enter [the return-leg of entrusted power](A29-prime-Return-or-Extraction.md), so the recovered purpose can govern the next use.

The musical distinction between operational and telic return also prevents the circuit from making its own continuation an end. A task can finish. A model can be retired. Recognition of the relation in which an instrument serves a purpose can release the demand to keep the instrument busy. The capacity for another act remains without requiring an endless sequence of outputs to establish its worth.

## #5→0 — A changed beginning

A completed passage returns something specific: corrected information, a revised model, an altered criterion, a changed commission or renewed reasons for retaining a fitting condition. These can occur together, but none is established by naming the others. The next act inherits the actual judgment under the authority and material conditions that let it matter. Where altered processing is claimed, the producing relation must actually change; a reaffirmed fitting rule has its different consequence in what the next act can now receive under it.

An act [distinguishes within a source-field, forms a determination and turns its achieved form toward its source](../A18-Primordial-Symbolon-and-Its-Eight-Determinations.md). A technical result is one determinate articulation of that field. Its sourceward return retains the conditions by which it could be produced and the encounters capable of changing it.

[Manifestation into an achieved determination and its sourceward return](AC.md) give the act two directions: formation brings forth a result, and return makes its determining relation available through that result. In the relay, this becomes a practical demand to keep the formation of a result accessible at the grain required by its consequences. A later agent or person can then receive more than an answer: they can receive the means of discovering what would change it.
